analysis.title: GS US TMT .. quick hits ..
key_insights: Broad market held up on 10/22 with about 67% of S&P 500 members higher and the equal-weight S&P up 73 bps, while the NDX closed down 290 bps, its worst day since mid-June. The NDX is now lower on 9 of the last 12 sessions.
The S&P ex-AI index has just passed the S&P 500 in YTD performance.

Desk flows skewed to sellers, with no sign of anyone playing offense in AI or Semis. Client conversations focused on what drove the move (oil, earnings sell-the-news in META, LRCX and TTMI, or positioning) and on what would turn the story around.

Clients named the election, easing macro headwinds and AI datapoints or thematic momentum as possible sources of relief. The desk says there are too many overhangs to play offense in a truncated calendar window with FOMC, earnings and the election close.

The desk sees the market as open to new, non-AI, idiosyncratic TMT ideas for the first time in a long while, citing the recent move in consumer stocks. Names drawing inbounds: SPOT, DIS, FOXA, LYV, TTWO, RBLX, ABNB, V, MA, NOW, ZS, SPHR and AAPL.

There was a clear rotation from cyclicals into defensives, attributed to oil retracing to cycle highs with no relief yet, and to the AI-driven selloff pushing the market to reassess longer-term growth expectations.

The SAP print and reaction drew little debate. The desk reads that as a sign of subtly improving, less polarized Software sentiment, and some clients asked whether IBM is worth a look if the Software re-acceleration story plays out. NOW and MSFT report next.
After-hours AI datapoints were firm: FIX backlog rose $3.8bn q/q, WDC guided to 16-17% q/q revenue growth, and MXL guided about 10% above the Street.
A number of AI and Semi stocks are now flat to down on the year, or up no more than about 10% YTD, including AVGO, QCOM, CRDO, SNPS, CDNS, TEL, SANM, TTMI, APH, DY, FN, MTZ and COHR.

The SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions since Mon 10/12, the biggest 9-day stretch of underperformance in 20+ years. The SOX is now testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025.
The NDX lagged the NDX equal-weight by about 138 bps on the day, a bottom-5 day in more than 10 years.
The GS broad-based AI basket is down about 24% from its local high, matching the July drawdown, and the low-vol factor has been strongly bid.

earnings_insights: SAP reported on 10/22 with a low-debate reaction, per the desk's conversations.
META fell 7%, LRCX fell 12% and TTMI fell 28% on 10/22 after earnings, described as sell-the-news or weakness. Figures are share-price moves, not EPS.
FIX posted after the close on 10/22: backlog up $3.8bn q/q, with management citing 'relentless demand'. The stock was down 3% after hours.
WDC posted after the close on 10/22 and guided to 16-17% q/q revenue growth, the best q/q growth this cycle. The stock was down 3% after hours.
MXL posted after the close on 10/22 and guided about 10% above the Street, up about 15% q/q. The stock was down 2% after hours.
NOW and MSFT are the next earnings reports in Software.

tension_points.bull_case: Clients look to the election, easing macro headwinds, or AI datapoints and thematic momentum for relief. After-hours prints from FIX, WDC and MXL showed strong demand and guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: The NDX fell 290 bps, the SOX is testing its 200-day moving average, the AI basket is down about 24%, and desk flows skew to sellers. Earnings have done little to stabilize things, and there are too many overhangs to play offense.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The SOX holding or breaking its 200-day moving average, and the election, FOMC and earnings calendar resolving the overhangs.
